title: Roadmap dependency ecosystem map and on-call handoff protocol
creator: Marcus Chen
description: Create a lightweight "ecosystem map" and an operational on-call handoff protocol that makes roadmap dependencies visible and actionable across Eng/Design/Security/Infra during cycle planning and execution. The deliverable is (1) a shared dependency graph + ownership catalog, (2) a short runbook for dependency-related pager rotations and handoffs, and (3) a telemetry contract (events and dashboards) so PMs can see blocker signal fidelity in the Console.
background: Current dependency tracking is fragmented: teams publish commitments in separate docs, design reviews in Figma, security tickets in the compliance tracker, and infra changes in CHANGELOGs. That fragmentation leads to late escalations during sprints and opaque ownership for cross-cutting rollback/mitigation decisions. Several recent cutovers (runtime-1.18 rollout and dedicated autoscaler changes) surfaced these gaps.
objective: Reduce time-to-resolution for cross-team blockers during a cycle by 40% and eliminate ambiguity on single-point ownership for top-20 roadmap dependencies. Provide PMs with a signal surface in Console to track dependency health per initiative.
success_metrics: Median time from dependency-blocker detection to owner acknowledgement <= 4 hours
Top-20 tracked dependencies have single named owner and fallback owner recorded
Dependency-related incidents per cycle reduced by 30% for participating initiatives
Console dashboard shows dependency liveness and stale-ack alerts for >90% of tracked items
acceptance_criteria: Published ecosystem map with dependency edges, owner, fallback, SLA (ack/TTR), and links to artifact(s)
A one-page runbook that describes: how to raise a dependency pager, triage steps, and escalation ladder
Telemetry contract documented (event names, required fields) and proof-of-concept stream to Console dashboards
Pilot run with three initiatives (runtime, console, private-deploy) completed and retrospective artifacts posted
stakeholders: Eng Leads: Priya Nair, Daniel Ortiz
risks: Teams may treat the map as static single-source-of-truth—needs owner-maintenance policy
Telemetry schema creep: adding too many fields will slow adoption—keep minimal viable contract
Pager fatigue if on-call responsibilities for dependency pages are unclear
Dependency ownership politics may require mediator involvement for some cross-organization components
